title: External Modules
bullets: Separate related code into Python files.

title: Why split a program into modules?
paragraphs: As a program grows, one large file becomes harder to read, test and maintain.
Keep related functions, classes and variables together in separate modules. Let the main program coordinate the overall flow.
A useful module can be reused in another program without copying all of its supporting code.

title: Create a module
paragraphs: A module is a Python file containing code that another program can use.
Save this function in math_tools.py. The file name becomes the module name: math_tools.
Defining a function does not call it. This file produces no printed output yet.

title: Import a function
paragraphs: Use from ... import ... to import a function from another module.
The function name is added to the current namespace, so you can call double_number(5) directly.
Keep both Python files in the same folder. Switch file tabs to inspect or edit either file.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
from math_tools import double_number

result = double_number(5)
print(result)

title: Two files, one program
paragraphs: main.py imports the function; math_tools.py defines it. Step follows execution between the files.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
from math_tools import double_number

result = double_number(5)
print(result)

title: Test a module directly
paragraphs: Python sets __name__ to "__main__" when a file is executed directly.
Put test calls inside this guard so you can check a module on its own.
Run math_tools.py directly: its test prints 10.

files.name: math_tools.py

title: Import without running the tests
paragraphs: On import, __name__ is math_tools. The guarded test is skipped; only main.py prints a result.

files.name: math_tools.py

title: One-way: perform an action
paragraphs: A value is passed into the function through a parameter.
The function performs an action without explicitly returning a result. Here it prints a greeting.
This lesson calls that pattern one-way parameter passing. A function without an explicit return value returns None.

title: Two-way: return a result
paragraphs: Parameters provide input; return sends a result back to the calling code.
The caller can store the result and use it elsewhere.
This lesson calls that pattern two-way parameter passing. Returning a value does not automatically change the caller’s original variable.
code:
def double_number(number):
    return number * 2

result = double_number(5)
print(result)

title: Document the module’s interface
paragraphs: Another programmer should be able to use a module without reading its entire implementation.
Document what each function does, what its parameters mean, and what it returns. Explain important assumptions, units or restrictions.
Use docstrings for descriptions and type hints to show the kinds of values a function expects and returns.

title: Type hints describe the interface

annotations.title: Parameters
annotations.text: length: float and width: float describe the expected input types.

annotations.title: Return value
annotations.text: -> float describes the expected result type.

annotations.title: A hint, not a check
annotations.text: Python does not enforce these types automatically at runtime.

title: Docstrings explain how to use a function
code:
def calculate_area(length, width):
    """Calculate the area of a rectangle.

    :param length: The length of the rectangle.
    :param width: The width of the rectangle.
    :return: The area of the rectangle.
    """
    return length * width

print(calculate_area(3.0, 4.0))

annotations.title: Description
annotations.text: The first line states what the function does.

annotations.title: Parameters
annotations.text: :param entries describe the meaning of each input.

annotations.title: Result
annotations.text: :return: describes the value sent back to the caller.

title: Try it with your own module
paragraphs: Create a geometry_tools.py module containing a documented function.
Import the function into main.py, pass in values, and use its return value.
Add a guarded test so the module can be checked directly without printing test output on import.
